nodes.name: Magnetic-field-assisted Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The vertical Co fibers scaffold was synthesized via a magnetic-field-assisted hydrothermal method based on the 'stacking growth mechanism'. As shown in Figure S1a (Supporting Information), the Co^{2+} in solution is first reduced by N2H4·H2O to Co particles with a size of 4-6 μm. Without the external magnetic field, the reduced Co particles spontaneously attach to each other randomly (Figure S1b, Supporting Information). However, in the presence of an external magnetic field, the reduced Co particles stack orderly along with a direction of the magnetic induction line to form a straight fiber-like morphology (Figure 1c,d). In view of these characteristics, the Co particles will nucleate on the surface of Ni foam and stack orderly to form parallel Co fibers arrays architecture (Figure 1b). As shown in the digital photo (Figure S2a, Supporting Information), the stacked Co fibers uniformly cover the Ni substrate with a radius of ≈5 cm.

nodes.name: Molten Lithium Infiltration
nodes.procedure: The Co fibers skeleton was immersed into molten lithium. Driven by the capillary action, molten lithium can easily infuse along the Co fibers scaffold and fill the gap among the fibers, thus forming a Li/Co composite anode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co fibers arrays show vertically aligned morphology with diameter ≈5 μm (Figure 1b-d). SFI@Li/Co cross-section shows uniform Li infilling and conformal SFI coating (Figure 1i-k).
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of b) Co fibers arrays: c) Cross-sectional image and d) Top-view images. ... From the cross-sectional SEM image (Figure 1i), it can be seen that the Co fibers matrix is sealed by Li metal.

nodes.characterization_summary: SFI@Li/Co SFI layer composed of 2-5 nm nanoparticles. HRTEM shows lattice fringes 0.204 nm (Li₂S (220)), 0.232 nm (LiF (111)), 0.201 nm (LiF (200)). SEAD shows polycrystalline rings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: m) TEM images and SEAD images of SFI@Li/Co anode. ... The high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) images also display clear lattice fringes, measured to be 0.204 nm, which can be indexed to (220) planes of Li₂S, as well as 0.232 and 0.201 nm, which can be attributed to the (111) and (200) crystal planes of LiF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co fibers: hexagonal Co (JCPDS 01-1278) peaks at 41.7°(100), 44.7°(002), 47.5°(101), 75.9°(110) (Figure S6a). SFI@Li/Co also shows Li metal peaks (Figure 2a).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) ... the Co fibers show characteristic peaks at 41.7°, 44.7°, 47.5°, and 75.9°, which are indexed well to the (100), (002), (101), and (110) crystal planes of hexagonal Co phase (JCPDS 01-1278).

nodes.characterization_summary: SFI layer shows F 1s peak at 684.8 eV (LiF), S 2p peaks at 160.3/161.6 eV (Li₂S) and 163.6 eV (Li₂S₂).
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution XPS spectra of F and S elements (Figure 2d,e), the characteristic peak of LiF (684.8 eV) can be observed in the F 1s spectrum. Meanwhile, for the spectrum of S 2p, the characteristic peaks of lithium sulfides including Li₂S and Li₂S₂ are detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: SFI@Li/Co shows Co in fiber shape, uniform distribution of S and F elements along fibers forming conformal SFI layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the electron dispersive spectrum (EDS) mapping images show (Figure 1l), the Co element depicts a shape of fiber, and S and F elements are uniformly distributed along with the fiber, forming a conformal and interacted SFI layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: SFI layer shows consecutive distribution of F, S, and Li elements with higher F concentration than S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notice that, on the whole, F and S elements are distributed along with Li element (Figure 2f-h). The difference is that the concentration distribution of F element is higher than S element because of its dominant amount in the plasma.
